video.titulo: The Only Earthquake Anyone Saw Coming - And Why It Never Happened Again
video.descricao:
Sources: https://tinyurl.com/critical23
Support the channel: https://payhip.com/b/GWENV

Earthquake prediction has worked exactly once; you will learn all about that in this video. 

On February 4th, 1975, a magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck Haicheng in Liaoning Province, in northeast China. 2,041 people died in a region where the toll should have been far higher, because one county walked its entire population outdoors before dark. Seventeen months later and 250 miles (400 km) away, Tangshan came apart at 3:42 in the morning with no warning at all. The official death toll is 242,769.

This is educational, not a prediction that an earthquake is imminent.

CHAPTERS
0:00 The Only Earthquake Prediction That Ever Worked
3:14 How 1975 China Trained a Country to Watch the Ground
6:07 501 Earthquakes in 36 Hours: The One Real Signal
9:44 8:15 in the Morning: One County Empties Itself
14:16 The Rewrite, and the 150,000 Lives Myth
15:44 Tangshan 1976: 242,769 Dead, No Foreshocks
17:19 Parkfield: The Prediction That Arrived 11 Years Late
18:37 Qinglong County: 7,000 Buildings Down, One Death
20:09 ShakeAlert Is Not Earthquake Prediction

Have you ever got an evacuation order and you didn't go? Tell me in the comments what your reason was.

Subscribe to Critical Latitude for more on earthquakes, faults, volcanoes and what the planet is actually doing. 

SOURCES AND DISCLAIMER
This video is built on the 2006 archive study by Kelin Wang and colleagues in the Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America, the U.S. Geological Survey's own position on earthquake prediction and its Parkfield experiment, the 2005 Nature paper on the 2004 Parkfield earthquake, the peer-reviewed lives-saved estimate published in Seismological Research Letters, the 1977 American delegation report on earthquake research in China, and the United Nations case study of Qinglong County. 

Every source is linked at the top of this description. 

This is educational history and science. It is not a prediction
